title: Quantity boundaries
brief: Bands that cover every quantity once: no gaps to fall through, no overlaps to argue about.
instructions: Classify 1 to 9 as small, 10 to 99 as medium, and 100 to 1000 as large. Return every item.
Return only the declared columns, in their declared order and exact SQL types, and follow the stated ordering contract. NULL placement is declared, not assumed.
starterExplanation: The starter reads order_item_id and qty out of order_items. It runs. It does not answer the question.

hints.text: Every permitted quantity must match exactly one branch of the CASE.
Either write closed intervals, or let increasing upper bounds do the work.
The extra items sit on 9, 10, 99 and 100, which is where careless bands fail.

dataClaims.sql: SELECT count(*)::VARCHAR FROM order_items WHERE qty IN (9, 10, 99, 100)
dataClaims.claim: hints[2]: extra items sit on quantities 9, 10, 99 and 100
